- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market correction.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +2–3% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overcorrection.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and adjust forecast downward.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; cap forecast at +1.5–2.0% above recent mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.67/1.00 values, model may be overfitting to recent trends; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to prevent momentum bias.
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 day lagged correction to avoid premature reversal.
